title: Bringing Those From Another Culture Into the Conversation
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece focuses on the isolation new team members from another culture often feel in a workplace, arguing that the real barrier isn't language alone but exclusion from the everyday, informal texture of team conversation. The author notes that even genuinely funny material often doesn't translate across cultures. The recommended intervention is deliberately creating shared conversational touchpoints so there's common material to talk about beyond work itself. The piece treats this as the necessary first step before addressing deeper cultural differences.
points: The core barrier for new team members from another culture isn't just language, it's exclusion from the informal texture of team conversation.
Humor doesn't reliably translate across cultures, compounding isolation in ways that formal onboarding alone doesn't fix.
Deliberately creating shared conversational touchpoints gives new colleagues something to talk about beyond work.
The piece treats conversational inclusion as the necessary first step before addressing deeper differences in feedback or recognition preferences.
quotes: Language differences are hard enough, but when news, events, popular shows, and various other matters team members talk about are both unknown and bewildering, new team members feel lost.
To make matters worse, what is funny in one culture is often not a point of amusement in another culture.
Aside from work tasks, new team members need something to talk about as a way of connecting to others.
Social events where team members and the new colleague can experience things together help to create a foundation for future conversations.
The best leaders know that it is always the quality of the conversation that matters most in producing acceptance and comfort in teams.
